elements.evidence: "Neither party shall solicit personnel of the other party directly involved in the Services"

elements.element: Scope limited to personnel directly involved in the Services
elements.evidence: "directly involved in the Services"; "the preceding sentence is limited to that same scope and period"

elements.element: Duration 12 months from the end of their involvement
elements.evidence: "for 12 months from the end of that involvement"; first sentence "for 12 months after the end of their involvement in the Services"
"does not restrict general advertisements not specifically targeted at the other party's employees"
"shall not solicit any Vendor personnel" — prior "solicit, hire, or employ" and "regardless of how the employee applies" deleted

elements.element: No non-solicit binding Customer at all
elements.evidence: "Customer shall not solicit any Vendor personnel" remains operative

offending_extra_words: and the preceding sentence is limited to that same scope and period
reasons: All six atomic fallback elements are met: mutuality, scope limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, 12 months from end of involvement, general-advertisement and unsolicited-approach carve-outs, and no no-hire (the deleted "hire, or employ" and "regardless of how the employee applies" confirm this). The clause sits at the fallback.
Preferred position (no non-solicit on Customer) is not achieved, as the Customer-facing covenant survives — acceptable given the locked fallback target.

Minimality fails only on the retro-fitting device: the replaced first sentence still restricts Customer as to "any Vendor personnel", and the inserted sentence then has to claw it back with "and the preceding sentence is limited to that same scope and period". Editing the first sentence to read "Vendor personnel directly involved in the Services" would have made that cross-reference unnecessary and avoided duplicated, overlapping covenants.
Intent is preserved: no undefined terms, no contradiction (the limiting clause reconciles the two sentences), and no unrelated commercial term is disturbed.
